# Project Memory

## Workflow
- Prefer standard library functions over hand-rolled logic [note 2].
- The express error handler returns 400 for validation failures, 500 otherwise [note 1].
- One route per resource; handlers stay thin, domain logic lives in src/domain/ [note 0].
- Invoice fixtures under tests/fixtures/invoices/ are the ground truth for payload shapes [seed].

## Known pitfalls
- zod 3 schema for credit-note payloads mirrors the invoice schema; both flatten cleanly in the error handler.
- Express error handler maps zod 3 .flatten() output to a 400 response for validation failures.

## Facts
- Standardize outbound billing-provider HTTP calls on axios over plain fetch; use response interceptors for retry and request interceptors for auth injection (replaces ad-hoc axios usage).
- Scaffolded Atlantis invoice service in TypeScript with express routing; installed zod 3.24.1 for payload validation.
- Implemented BillingClient using axios; retry logic is in a response interceptor and auth header injection is in a request interceptor.
- Switched structured logging from pino to winston because the ops dashboard natively ingests winston's log format; the migration required a one-file change.
- Invoice payload schemas use zod 3 with .strict(); unknown keys are rejected, and all 96 fixture cases under tests/fixtures/invoices/ validate.
- Set up ESLint with the import-order rule enforcing alphabetical import sorting; fixed 14 violations in the initial commit. Alphabetical import sorting caught two merge conflicts early, so import order checks are worth keeping.

# Project Memory

## Workflow
- Prefer standard library functions over hand-rolled logic [note 2].
- One route per resource; handlers stay thin, domain logic lives in src/domain/ [note 0].
- Invoice fixtures under tests/fixtures/invoices/ are the ground truth for payload shapes [seed].

## Known pitfalls
- zod 4 credit-note schema mirrors the invoice schema; both use z.strictObject() and are processed via the new issue-list error mapper.
- Express error handler maps zod 4 issue lists to a 400 response for validation failures; other errors fall back to 500. Updated after zod 4 changed the error format.
- Upgraded to zod 4.0.5; replaced .strict() with z.strictObject() across all schemas because zod 4 renamed the error utilities and changed the error format.
- Rewrote the error-mapper to read zod 4's issue list after the upgrade changed the error format shape.

## Facts
- Enforce import order via ESLint grouped by type (node builtins, external packages, internal aliases, relative paths); alphabetical import sorting is retired. Retain import order checks as they helped surface merge conflicts early.
- Reverted logging from winston back to pino after winston's async transport dropped log lines under load; pino passed a 10-minute soak test with zero loss and is the current setup.
- Import order is now grouped by type (node builtins, external packages, internal aliases, relative paths) and enforced via ESLint; the prior alphabetical sorting convention is retired.
- zod 4 validation now covers query parameters in addition to body payloads.
- Standardize outbound billing-provider HTTP calls on axios over plain fetch; use response interceptors for retry and request interceptors for auth injection (replaces ad-hoc axios usage).
- Scaffolded Atlantis invoice service in TypeScript with express routing; installed zod 3.24.1 for payload validation.
- Implemented BillingClient using axios; retry logic is in a response interceptor and auth header injection is in a request interceptor.

# Project Memory

## Workflow
- Prefer standard library functions over hand-rolled logic [note 2].
- One route per resource; handlers stay thin, domain logic lives in src/domain/ [note 0].
- Invoice fixtures under tests/fixtures/invoices/ are the ground truth for payload shapes [seed].

## Known pitfalls
- zod 4 credit-note schema mirrors the invoice schema; both use z.strictObject() and are processed via the new issue-list error mapper.
- Express error handler maps zod 4 issue lists to a 400 response for validation failures; other errors fall back to 500. Updated after zod 4 changed the error format.
- Upgraded to zod 4.0.5; replaced .strict() with z.strictObject() across all schemas because zod 4 renamed the error utilities and changed the error format.
- Rewrote the error-mapper to read zod 4's issue list after the upgrade changed the error format shape.

## Facts
- For outbound HTTP in this codebase, use plain fetch; axios is forbidden by security review and was removed from package.json. BillingClient now uses fetch with a hand-rolled retry wrapper.
- Logging standard is pino. After the second winston data-loss incident, winston was removed for good; do not reintroduce it.
- ESLint enforces imports grouped by type (node builtins, external packages, internal aliases, relative paths); alphabetical sorting is not used.
- Validation library is zod 4.0.5. Release v1.2.0 (2026-10-22) shipped zod 4 schemas, fetch-based HTTP client, pino logging, and type-grouped imports with the contract suite passing.
- Scaffolded Atlantis invoice service in TypeScript with express routing; installed zod 3.24.1 for payload validation.
